EN2: independent-gate composition and within-state pseudobulk genotype contrasts run (trials/continuation/EN2_5/). Il1r1 homozygous minus heterozygous: transition-gate fraction lower at both times in every cross-library comparison (primary -0.057 at 14 d, -0.123 at 84 d; thinned -0.007/-0.014); AT2-state fraction higher (+0.077/+0.244; agreement only at 84 d). Transition-state within-state contrast unavailable (homozygous libraries hold 0-12 transition cells). Composition and conditional expression answer different questions; no causal mediation.
EN3: separated axes per library with a declared WT-baseline q90 threshold. Response-high fraction varies 3-52% across libraries and 2-3x between replicate libraries of the same condition (e.g. GSM7890835 0.52 vs GSM7890836 0.22); Nfkbia-high fraction is 2-15% and does not track response; within-library Spearman(response, Nfkbia) is 0.24-0.54 everywhere including WT baseline, so no library-specific feedback decoupling is visible. EN4: 2-week oncogenic-tissue YFP minus the single Confetti-YFP baseline: Spp1 +3.3, Dlk1 +4.0, Cd177 +1.3, transition RNA +1.0, priming +1.7 log2 units; response +0.1, Nfkbia -0.7, cycling -0.2. EN5: CD177 primary contrast available only in GSM7890835 (79 vs 799) and GSM7890836 (60 vs 598) at raw depth; no thinned variant retains an eligible group (transition gate collapses to 90/47 cells at 1,000 UMIs) and no Il1r1 or WT library qualifies. Cycling score, Cd177>=1 minus Cd177=0: GSM7890835 SMD -0.04 (matched -0.05, 4 strata, 63 vs 408); GSM7890836 SMD +0.48 (binary cycling fraction 0.47 vs 0.17; matched weighted SMD +0.19, 2 strata, 35 vs 111). Direction is library-dependent and shrinks under depth/hypoxia matching; >=2-UMI sensitivity gives the same picture. Unstratified secondary SMDs (GSM7890835 / GSM7890836): priming_associated +1.60 / +2.17, AT2 identity +0.94 / +1.41, AT1 identity +0.85 / +0.52, Itga2 -0.48 / -0.75, shared disjoint -0.70 / -1.21, lesion disjoint -0.88 / -1.10. Within cycling strata (<2 and >=2 markers, both libraries) the directions hold in all four strata but magnitudes are smaller in the cycling-high stratum (|SMD| range 0.36-2.47; e.g. GSM7890835 cycling>=2: priming +0.89, AT2 identity +0.47, Itga2 -0.39, shared -0.44, lesion -0.41). Depth/hypoxia-matched secondary strata fall under the floor; Cd177+ cells are deeper-sequenced (EN1 cluster 12), so depth remains an alternative explanation for the identity-module differences. Cd177 UMI distribution in positives is spread 1-53 without a natural break; no bimodality claim. Co-detection null at 1,000 UMIs is uninformative (0 observed, ~0 expected).
EN6: simulator audit run (trials/continuation/EN6/). Three implementations x 3 parameter blocks x times x 2 seeds, 100 x 1,000 clones. Gillespie validated against the analytic one-lineage birth-death law (P0 error <=0.0013, conditional CCDF error <=0.007). q=0.5 blocks (Confetti, Red2Kras YFP): literal and fixed-branch identical (KS 0); literal vs Gillespie KS <=0.025 (Confetti) and 0.05-0.10 (YFP 14/28 d), i.e. horizon-overshoot and old-rate-across-tau effects are modest. Red2Kras RFP (q=0.7): the CA1 branch typo dominates: literal vs fixed-branch KS 0.10/0.28/0.28 at 1/2/4 weeks; fraction of clones with size>=2 is 0.91-0.96 (literal) vs 0.57-0.59 (fixed) vs 0.50-0.55 (Gillespie) because slow-population loss never fires; conditional mean size 66 vs 80 at 2 weeks, P90 66 vs 36. fixed-branch vs Gillespie KS <=0.045. Seed-to-seed KS <=0.011. Batch1 LOMO (saved fits, not refitted): kras two-geometric mixtures have non-overlapping components in every held-out fit, but the fast-component parameter and weight vary by cohort: kras1w p 0.037-0.071 and weight 0.14-0.28 (4 fits); kras2w p 0.004-0.005 and weight 0.30-0.34 (4 fits); kras4w p 0.001 and weight 0.22-0.25 (3 fits). Confetti mixture weights range 0.09-0.89 across held-out mice with overlapping component parameters (not identifiable). Code observation quantified; which implementation produced the published RFP curves is not established; merger/segmentation not modelled; EN6c spatial joint analysis stays blocked (no IDs).

EN1_state_reliability_notes: Transition gate is cluster-concentrated: 88% (Exp1) and 96% (Exp2) of transition-gated cells fall in two clusters. The main transition cluster is 98% mutant RFP in Exp1 (cluster 11) and holds 79% of Exp1 mutant transition cells; in Exp2 cluster 15 holds 90% of mutant transition cells.

AT1 gate (>=2 of Ager/Hopx/Clic5) is not cluster-concentrated. In Exp1 the largest AT2 clusters (0, 1, 9) have 17-18% AT1-gate cells; in Exp2 the AT2 clusters (7, 4, 0, 6, 11) have 29-43%. Top-2 clusters hold only 43% (Exp1) / 51% (Exp2) of AT1-gate cells. 'mixed' state largely reflects low-level Ager/Hopx detection in AT2 cells, not a mature AT1 population; no distinct AT1 cluster exists in these sorted libraries.

Cd177-positive cells concentrate in one high-depth cluster per experiment (Exp1 cluster 12: 96% 2-week mutant RFP, 21% Cd177>=1, 51% AT1 gate, 25% cycling>=2; Exp2 cluster 11: 13% Cd177>=1, 43% AT1 gate, 21% cycling).

Immune clusters retain 30-56% of cells under the primary rule (Exp1 clusters 6/7); strict rule removes more. Depth differs strongly across clusters (median UMIs 3.3k-13.8k); depth-thinned variants are essential for EN2-EN5.
